newsitem.title: FRANCE: French coal miners occupy offices in protest.
newsitem.headline: French coal miners occupy offices in protest.

text.p: Coalminers from the southeastern French town of La Mure have taken over regional government offices in Grenoble in protest at state plans to shut down the area's mines, officials said on Monday.
They said 30 miners occupied regional industry and research offices on Monday morning to pressure the state to continue mining in La Mure on a reduced scale until 2005.
Current plans are for the La Mure mines to close down in March. The workers argue that the mines could remain open past March by mining slag rather than coal.
A government-appointed mediator has launched talks on the miners' demands.

The tactic of occupying government offices to press labour demands is becoming increasingly popular in France where unemployment is at a record 12.7 percent and the government is intent on holding the line on state spending.

Employees of the Credit Foncier bank have been occupying the property lender's Paris headquarters since January 17 in protest at state plans to dismantle it. The workers held the bank's governor hostage for the first five days of the protest.
